questions.question: Describe shell, frame and solid structures, stating where each gets its strength, with one natural and one man-made example of each.
questions.expected_answer: A shell is a thin, usually curved, continuous skin that spreads loads over its whole surface; strength comes from shape; natural example an egg or tortoise shell, man-made a car body or dome. A frame is a skeleton of members joined at nodes with open spaces between; strength comes from the arrangement, especially triangles; natural example a skeleton or tree, man-made a pylon, roof truss or cell phone tower. A solid gets its strength from the mass of material in it; natural example a boulder or cliff, man-made a dam wall or brick wall.

questions.question: Explain why adding a diagonal to a rectangular frame makes it rigid, and distinguish tension from compression in frame members.
questions.expected_answer: A rectangle of members pinned at the corners can change shape into a parallelogram under a sideways push without any member changing length. A diagonal divides it into two triangles, and a triangle cannot change shape unless a side changes length, so the frame becomes rigid; this is triangulation. A member in tension is being stretched and can be thin, like a tie or cable; a member in compression is being squashed and must be thicker to avoid buckling, like a strut.

questions.question: Give the main strengths and weaknesses of solid structures and explain how a cell phone tower and a house combine structure types.
questions.expected_answer: Solids resist crushing and being pushed over and withstand knocks and weather, but they are heavy, use a lot of material and are poor at spanning, so a long solid beam fails under its own weight and a wall needs a lintel over an opening. A cell phone tower is a frame of triangulated steel standing on a solid concrete foundation, with shell covers over the antennas. A house has solid foundations and walls, a frame roof of trusses and a shell water tank, each type chosen for the loads that part carries.
